data.name: Bibhuti
data.gender_notes: Bibhuti is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Bibhuti is a Sanskrit word derived from the root bibhuh meaning 'auspicious' or 'divine substance'. In Hindu mythology, Bibhuti is a sacred substance made from the ashes of sacred fires, used in religious rituals and ceremonies. It represents purity, auspiciousness, and the presence of the divine. The name Bibhuti carries the meaning “Auspicious, Divine Substance” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bibhuti usually hope their child will grow to embody auspicious, divine substance and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Bibhuti belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Auspicious, Divine Substance.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bibhuti total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: In Hindu culture, Bibhuti holds deep significance in various rituals and ceremonies, particularly those related to worship of gods and goddesses, cremation of the dead, and purification process. It is often used to decorate idols of deities, smear on the body of the devotee during rituals, or also sprinkle in the air during puja or homa. Consuming Bibhuti during rituals is believed to purify the mind and body and bring good luck and prosperity.
data.spiritual_significance: Bibhuti holds immense spiritual significance as it symbolizes the divine presence of the deity in the material world. The use of Bibhuti in Hindu religious practices is a way to remind us of the transcendental reality beyond material existence. It also reminds us of the significance of purification of the mind, body, and soul to align ourselves with the divine. By using Bibhuti, we invite the divine essence into our lives and can connect with the higher consciousness.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bibhuti symbolizes the divine presence and transformation within an individual. It is a Sanskrit word meaning 'sacred ash', representing the purifying and enlightening effects of spiritual practices and self-realization.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Bibhuti was a courtier in the court of King Harshavardhana during the 7th century. The name Bibhuti carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: King Harshavardhana was a powerful king who ruled over a large part of northern India during the 7th century. Bibhuti was one of his trusted courtiers.
